The '''Oswald Veblen Prize in Geometry''' is an award granted by the [[American Mathematical Society]] for notable research in [[geometry]] or [[topology]].  It was funded in 1961 in memory of [[Oswald Veblen]] and first issued in 1964.  The Veblen Prize is now worth US$5000, and is awarded every three years.

The first seven prize winners were awarded for works in topology. [[James Harris Simons|Jim Simons]] and [[William Thurston]] were the first ones to receive it for works in geometry.<ref name="DurenAskey1989">{{cite book|editor1=Peter L. Duren|editor2=Richard Askey|editor3=Uta C. Merzbach|editor3-link= Uta Merzbach |title=A Century of Mathematics in America, Part II|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Eq5072shy9AC&pg=PA521|date=January 1989|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|isbn=978-0-8218-0130-7|page=521}}</ref> As of 2025, there have been thirty-nine prize recipients.

==List of recipients==
Source: ''Notices of the American Mathematical Society''
* 1964 [[Christos Papakyriakopoulos]], for his papers<ref name="MacTutor">{{MacTutor|class=Honours|id=AMSVeblenPrize|title=Oswald Veblen Prize of the AMS}}</ref>
::"On solid tori",<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Papakyriakopoulos |first=Christos |date=1957 |title=On solid tori |journal=[[Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society]] |volume=3 |issue=7 |pages=281–299 |doi=10.1112/plms/s3-7.1.281}}</ref> and
::"On Dehn's lemma and the asphericity of knots".<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Papakyriakopoulos |first=Christos |date=1957 |title=On Dehn's lemma and the asphericity of knots |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |volume=66 |issue=1 |pages=1–26 |doi=10.2307/1970113 |jstor=1970113}}</ref>
* 1964 [[Raoul Bott]], for his papers<ref name="MacTutor" />
::"The space of loops on a Lie group",<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bott |first=Raoul |date=1958 |title=The space of loops on a Lie group |doi=10.1307/mmj/1028998010 | doi-access=free |journal=[[Michigan Mathematical Journal]] |volume=5 |issue=1 |pages=35–61}}</ref> and
::"The stable homotopy of the classical groups".<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bott |first=Raoul |date=1959 |title=The stable homotopy of the classical groups |journal=Annals of Mathematics |volume=70 |issue=2 |pages=313–337 |doi=10.2307/1970106 |jstor=1970106}}</ref>

* 1966 [[Morton Brown]] and [[Barry Mazur]] "for their work on the generalized Schoenflies theorem."<ref name="MacTutor" />
* 1971 [[Robion Kirby]], for his paper<ref name="MacTutor" />
::"Stable homeomorphisms and the annulus conjecture".<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kirby |first=Robion C. |date=1969 |title=Stable homeomorphisms and the annulus conjecture |journal=Annals of Mathematics |volume=89 |issue=3 |pages=575–582 |doi=10.2307/1970652 |jstor=1970652}}</ref>
* 1971 [[Dennis Sullivan]] for his work on the Hauptvermutung summarized in the paper<ref name="MacTutor" />
*::"On the Hauptvermutung for manifolds".<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Sullivan |first=Dennis P. |date=1967 |title=On the Hauptvermutung for manifolds |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/bulletin-of-the-american-mathematical-society/volume-73/issue-4/On-the-Hauptvermutung-for-manifolds/bams/1183528965.full |journal=[[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]] |volume=73 |issue=4 |pages=598–600}}</ref>
* 1976 [[William Thurston]] "for his work on foliations".<ref name="MacTutor" />
* 1976 [[James Harris Simons|James Simons]] "for his work on minimal varieties and characteristic forms".<ref name="MacTutor" />
* 1981 [[Mikhail Gromov (mathematician)|Mikhail Gromov]] "for his work relating topological and geometric properties of Riemannian manifolds."<ref name="gromov">{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/198102/198102FullIssue.pdf|title=Veblen Prizes for 1981|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|volume=28|issue=2|date=February 1981|pages=160–164}}</ref>

* 1981 [[Shing-Tung Yau]] "for his work in nonlinear partial differential equations, his contributions to the topology of differentiable manifolds, and for his work on the complex Monge-Ampère equation on compact complex manifolds."<ref name="gromov" />

* 1986 [[Michael Freedman]] "for his work in differential geometry and, in particular, the solution of the four-dimensional Poincaré conjecture."<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/198603/198603FullIssue.pdf|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|title=Michael H. Freedman Awarded 1986 Veblen Prize|volume=33|issue=2|date=March 1986|pages=227–228}}</ref>

* 1991 [[Andrew Casson]] "for his work on the topology of low-dimensional manifolds."<ref name="taub">{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/199103/199103FullIssue.pdf|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|date=March 1991|volume=38|issue=3|title=1991 Oswald Veblen Prize in Geometry|pages=181–183}}</ref>

* 1991 [[Clifford Taubes]] "for his foundational work in Yang-Mills theory."<ref name="taub" />

Hamilton]] "for his continuing study of the Ricci flow and related parabolic equations for a Riemannian metric."<ref name="hamtian">{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/199603/comm-veblen.pdf|title=1996 Oswald Veblen Prize|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|date=March 1996|volume=43|issue=3|pages=325–327}}.</ref>
